## Ecological Background

Roe deer (*Capreolus capreolus*) are widespread across Europe and are expanding their range under warming climate and land-use change (Danilov et al., 2017; Valente et al., 2014). With an average body mass of ~20–30 kg (Andersen et al., 1998; Pettorelli et al., 2002), they forage across woodland and agricultural edges, with tree sapling shoots forming a significant share of their diet (Tixier & Duncan, 1996).

Silver fir (*Abies alba*) is among the most preferred tree species for browsing, and sustained pressure can lead to regeneration failure (Senn & Suter, 2003). Here roe deer populate the landscape at a constant density of 14 individuals per 100 ha, with consumption parameterized from empirical feeding studies (Drozdz & Osiecki, 1973; Tixier & Duncan, 1996).

## Model Implementation

Instead of spatial spread via `BiteDispersal`, roe deer use `BiteDistribution` to introduce the agent evenly across coarse 1000 m (100 ha) cells. Carrying capacity in `BiteBiomass` aggregates the foliage mass of all Silver fir saplings below 1.3 m height (`species=abal and height<1.3`).

Impact uses the `browsing` target, stopping current-year height growth of leader shoots for the fraction `agentImpact/hostBiomass` of eligible saplings.
